## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization of loop1 combined with a fused scatter loop2 can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Cache saturation
At q=0, ns/p falls from 7.022 (N=4000) to 5.962 (N=16000) as overhead amortizes; the L1d spill at N≈963 sits below the smallest measured point. Cost stays flat at ~5.83 from N=16000 through N=262000, crossing the L2→DRAM spill at N≈61680 with no knee. A slight rise to 6.37 at N=4M suggests TLB pressure. Death rate raises the floor monotonically (5.83→7.0→7.8→9.97→13.6 ns/p at q=0 through 0.5) without altering the N-shape — every curve is flat from N=16000 onward, confirming per-particle churn, not cache effects.

## Bandwidth
Peak is 11.67 GB/s at N=262000, q=0 — 46% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. Overhead-bound: PMC at N=1M, q=0 shows 59.1% useful, 23.2% processing, 17.7% discarded, 0.1% delivery. Near-zero delivery stalls and 17.7% discarded cycles indicate branchy scatter logic, not memory, is the limiter. Bandwidth falls with death rate — 11.67 (q=0) → 9.71 (q=0.05) → 6.82 (q=0.25) → 4.98 GB/s (q=0.5) — as spawn calls and respawn branching consume cycles.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized loop1 component-wise, not across particles: `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` operate on four float components of one particle, with `ext.16b` and `mov.s v17[3]` rearranging lanes. A single `ld1.s {v16}[1]` is an indexed element load — a mini-gather. Loop2 is entirely scalar: 16 `strb` and 12 `ldrb` perform byte-granular framebuffer writes with `csel` clamping to 0xff; `bfi` packs pixel indices. The scatter's byte stores and per-channel branching explain both the 46% ceiling cap and the 17.7% discarded cycles.

## Verdict
Refuted — peak is 11.67 GB/s (46% of ceiling) at q=0, and the fused scatter's 16 `strb` byte stores with per-channel `csel` clamping cannot stream regardless of death rate. The 17.7% discarded cycles confirm branchiness, not bandwidth, is the limiter. Loop1 auto-vectorizes component-wise (`fmul.4s`, `fadd.4s`) but the scalar loop2 scatter caps throughput under half the ceiling, falling to 6.82 GB/s (27%) by q=0.25.
